title: The World Cup Arrives in Santa Clara on Wednesday. It May Never Be This Close Again.
excerpt: When the USA faces Bosnia and Herzegovina at Levi’s Stadium on July 1, the knockout stage comes to the doorstep of one of the largest Indian-American communities in the United States.
body:
The FIFA World Cup has been played in Mexico City, Seattle, Houston, and Los Angeles over the past two weeks. On Wednesday evening, it comes to Santa Clara, California — and for the hundreds of thousands of Indian Americans who call the Bay Area home, it may be the closest a World Cup knockout match ever gets.

The United States will face Bosnia and Herzegovina in the Round of 32 at Levi’s Stadium — rebranded as the San Francisco Bay Area Stadium for the duration of the tournament — at 5 PM Pacific on July 1. Kickoff will happen roughly five miles from Apple’s headquarters, eight miles from the Google campus, and a short BART-and-shuttle ride from downtown San Francisco.

## A Tournament on Their Doorstep

The Bay Area has always been one of the most significant Indian-American population centres in the United States. Santa Clara County alone is home to more than 200,000 people of Indian origin, according to census estimates. Sunnyvale, Cupertino, Milpitas, and Fremont — all within a half-hour drive of the stadium — have some of the highest concentrations of South Asian residents anywhere in the country.

For many in this community, the 2026 World Cup has been an experience unlike any sporting event before it. India is not playing — it failed to qualify for the second-ever 48-team tournament — but that has not stopped the diaspora from engaging with the competition. Television ratings from the first two weeks show that India accounts for one of the largest global viewing audiences for the World Cup, a remarkable figure for a nation that did not send a team.


![Mexico City — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Sobrevuelos_CDMX_HJ2A4913_%2825514321687%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/3840px-Sobrevuelos_CDMX_HJ2A4913_%2825514321687%29_%28cropped%29.jpg)



> **"India is not playing — it failed to qualify for the second-ever 48-team tournament — but that has not stopped the diaspora from engaging with the competition."**



The NRI community in the United States has driven much of that viewership. Group-stage watch parties have been held in desi restaurants and community centres from Edison, New Jersey, to Sunnyvale, California. Many Indian Americans have adopted the host nation as their team, while others have rallied behind Argentina, Brazil, or whichever side happens to be playing that night.

## The USA’s Path So Far

Mauricio Pochettino’s side topped Group D with wins over Paraguay and Australia before falling 3-2 to Turkey in a meaningless final group match at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles on Thursday. The Americans had already clinched first place and rested most of their starters. Turkey scored a stoppage-time winner through Kaan Ayhan, but the result changed nothing in the standings.

The USA now faces Bosnia and Herzegovina, who finished third in Group B after beating Qatar 3-1 to secure one of the eight best third-place finishes. The Americans opened as heavy favourites, listed at -225 on the moneyline, with Bosnia at +650 for a regulation-time upset.

If the USA wins on Wednesday, the knockout path stays on the West Coast. Their Round of 16 match would be on Monday, July 6 at Lumen Field in Seattle, followed by a potential quarterfinal back in Inglewood at SoFi Stadium on July 10.


![Los Angeles — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Hollywood_Sign_%28Zuschnitt%29.jpg/3840px-Hollywood_Sign_%28Zuschnitt%29.jpg)


## Why This Match Matters to the Diaspora

There are practical reasons this game is significant. Tickets to World Cup knockout matches are among the most sought-after in world sport, and having one played in your metropolitan area eliminates the cost and logistics of cross-country travel. For families in the South Bay who might not fly to Dallas or New York for a match, Wednesday represents a rare chance to witness the tournament in person.

But there is a deeper significance, too. The Indian-American community in the Bay Area has grown up around technology and cricket. Football was not the sport many arrived with, but it has become the sport their children play in local youth leagues, the sport that fills weekend mornings at Baylands Park in Sunnyvale, the sport that connects immigrant families to the broader American experience.

The World Cup landing in Santa Clara is, in a sense, a reflection of how far that integration has come. A generation ago, the idea of the biggest sporting event on the planet being played five minutes from the curry houses of El Camino Real would have seemed absurd. Now it is a five-day reality.

## How to Watch

USA vs Bosnia and Herzegovina kicks off at 5 PM Pacific / 8 PM Eastern on Wednesday, July 1, at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara. The match will be broadcast on Fox, with streaming available on Fubo and Peacock (in Spanish). Tickets are available through FIFA’s official portal, though secondary-market prices have climbed steadily since the matchup was confirmed.

The Bay Area’s World Cup moment will be brief. After Wednesday, the tournament moves on. But for the Indian Americans who have watched this competition from their living rooms for decades, the next best thing to India qualifying may simply be the World Cup showing up in their backyard.
